stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Move the $R$, $L$, and $C$ sliders. Watch the resonant bell shift and change width. The two purple markers sit on the cut-off frequencies $f_L$ and $f_H$ (where $|H| = -3\,\text{dB}$). The bandwidth is $\Delta f = f_H - f_L$. Advance after visiting at least $3$ different $\Delta f$ decades.
stages.concept: A series RLC band-pass has resonant frequency $f_0 = 1/(2\pi\sqrt{L\,C})$ and quality factor $Q = (1/R)\sqrt{L/C} = f_0/\Delta f$. In dB: $|H|_{\text{dB}} = -10\,\log_{10}\!\bigl(1 + Q^2(f/f_0 - f_0/f)^2\bigr)$. Peak $0\,\text{dB}$ at $f_0$; the two $-3\,\text{dB}$ crossings give $f_L$ and $f_H$, with $\Delta f = R/(2\pi\,L)$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Adjust $R$, $L$, and $C$ so the bandwidth matches the target width $\Delta f = 200\,\text{Hz}$ (dashed orange span between the two orange lines). Many combinations work — you need $R/L = 2\pi\,\Delta f$.
stages.concept: Bandwidth depends only on $R$ and $L$: $\Delta f = R/(2\pi\,L)$. $C$ shifts the centre $f_0$ but not the width. For $\Delta f = 200\,\text{Hz}$: $R/L = 2\pi\cdot 200 \approx 1257\,\text{s}^{-1}$. E.g. $R = 126\,\Omega$ with $L = 100\,\text{mH}$, or $R = 12.6\,\Omega$ with $L = 10\,\text{mH}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Component values are hidden. Read the bandwidth $\Delta f$ directly from the Bode plot — it is the width of the bell at the $-3\,\text{dB}$ level, i.e. $\Delta f = f_H - f_L$. Answer every question correctly in one pass.
stages.concept: Reading $\Delta f$: locate the two frequencies where the bell crosses $-3\,\text{dB}$ (the horizontal orange line). Read them off the log x-axis, then subtract. On a log axis, equal visual spacing means equal factors, not equal differences — mind the ticks.

labels.question: question
labels.evaluate_prompt: Component values hidden. Read the bandwidth Δf from the Bode plot alone.
labels.tip1: R↑ or L↓ widens Δf ;  Δf = R/(2π·L)
labels.tip2: tune R/L until the bell width matches the orange span
labels.tip3: read Δf where |H| = −3 dB — all questions must pass
labels.peek_tip_1: Δf is the width of the bell at the −3 dB level. Find where the curve crosses the orange line on both sides and read the x-axis.
labels.peek_tip_2: The peak sits at f_0 (0 dB). Drop by 3 dB and mark the two frequencies. Δf = f_H − f_L.
labels.peek_tip_3: The x-axis is a log scale — the visual midpoint between f_L and f_H is not (f_L+f_H)/2 but √(f_L·f_H) ≈ f_0.

1.1: The two purple dots mark f_L and f_H. Slide R or L and watch the bell get wider or narrower.
1.2: Δf = R/(2π·L). Bigger R or smaller L widens the pass-band. C moves the centre f_0 but keeps the width fixed.
1.3: To visit 3 decades of Δf: try R = 10 Ω with L = 100 mH (narrow), then R = 100 Ω with L = 10 mH (medium), then R = 1 kΩ with L = 1 mH (wide).

2.1: You need Δf = 200 Hz. Only R and L matter: R/L = 2π·200 ≈ 1257 s⁻¹.
2.2: Pick a round L then compute R. L = 100 mH gives R = 1257·0.1 ≈ 126 Ω. C shifts f_0 but not the width — put it anywhere sensible.
2.3: Or L = 10 mH with R = 12.6 Ω. Or L = 1 H with R = 1257 Ω. Any C works; try C = 1 µF for a comfortable centre frequency.

3.1: Find where the bell curve crosses the horizontal −3 dB reference line — on the left and on the right.
3.2: Read the x-axis at both crossings: those are f_L and f_H. Then Δf = f_H − f_L.
3.3: Careful with the log axis: each big tick is ×10. A crossing halfway between two big ticks is ~×3, not ×5.
